A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same N2M research work. Their main text, equations, figures, results, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial restructuring in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original RoboCasa experiments, real-world Lamp Retrieval success rates, qualitative robot demonstrations, and a viewpoint-augmentation ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds a comparative benchmark, a real-world sequential task with human comparisons, and additional ablations.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the Point-BERT–MLP Gaussian-mixture predictor, successful-rollout supervision, regularized likelihood loss, viewpoint augmentation, and collision-free pose sampling. v2 elaborates the existing collision-checking step and evaluates alternative encoders and augmentations as ablations; it does not establish a replacement of the proposed N2M procedure.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation to a real-world sequence requiring navigation, chip-box pickup, further navigation, and disposal into a trash bin (Section 6.2). This substantially extends task requirements beyond individual manipulation transitions. The original RoboCasa tasks and five real-world scenarios remain, with four qualitative scenarios moved to Appendix D.1.3.

E2.justification: Mobi-π changes from a cited alternative in v1 to an evaluated comparator in v2's Table 1. v2 also adds a Human-Intuition baseline for the sequential task. Reachability and Oracle remain; the new benchmark uses a more rigorous IK- and collision-based Reachability implementation. MoTo and MoManipVLA are not separately evaluated implementations.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a CloseDrawer benchmark using BC Transformer and Mobi-π's diffusion-policy checkpoint, with success, human-labor, and inference-time measures. It also introduces a randomized 20-trial sequential-task protocol, separate policy-training budgets, and controlled encoder/augmentation comparisons. These are added protocols; the original four-task applicability experiment retains its stated 300-trial evaluation.

E4.justification: The original viewpoint-augmentation ablation is expanded with an augmented-view-count sweep, positional/noise augmentation removals, pretrained-versus-untrained Point-BERT, and PointNet++/PTV3 comparisons (Appendix D.2, Figures 15–16). These test which design choices drive performance. Appendix D.4 additionally reports qualitative failure observations, without presenting a controlled failure-rate benchmark.

E5.justification: v1 presents point estimates without uncertainty displays. v2 adds error bars and shaded bands to simulation and ablation plots, reports ± values in Table 1, and specifies six independent experiments of 50 trials for the new benchmark. The dispersion measures and seed counts remain undefined; additional runs for the retained experiments are not established.

E6.justification: Table 1 newly reports N2M success of 0.55±0.07 under DP versus Mobi-π's 0.24±0.05, and inference times of 0.07±0.03 versus 273.52±13.06 seconds. Figure 8 adds 12/20 completed sequences for N2M, versus 3/20 for Reachability and 5/20 for Human. Several retained Figure 5 scores also change. The new benchmark results are distinct experiments, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The Gaussian-mixture definition, likelihood objective, and three regularization terms in Equations 1–3 are mathematically unchanged apart from notation. Neither version provides formal theorems or proofs; v2's additional mechanism discussions are explanatory rather than new formal results.

C1.justification: v1 principally claims an effective, broadly applicable transition module with strong data efficiency and generalization. v2's abstract, contributions, and conclusion explicitly claim a systematic reformulation of base positioning and state-of-the-art performance against policy-aware and geometric alternatives, including inference-speed superiority. This strengthens the central comparative claims beyond the original effectiveness claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for Mobi-π's benchmark performance, sequential error compounding, and PTV3's architectural mismatch. It newly discusses failures involving small objects, distant viewpoints, noisy sensing, and limited manipulation policies. The conclusion replaces v1's RGB-only and failed-rollout future directions with active-learning implications and positioning N2M as complementary to intrinsic policy improvement.

D1.justification: v2 adds collision-check implementation details, benchmark GPU/CPU specifications, Pinocchio-based baseline details, and collection/training/inference timing accounting that distinguishes assumed overheads from measurements. Appendix C.6 documents the sequential task's demonstrations, randomization, M=300 augmentation, 150 training epochs, and human participants. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's robot, sensor, and augmentation descriptions.

R1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites research positioning around geometric methods versus policy-aware positioning, identifying Mobi-π as the sole existing policy-aware alternative. It removes much of v1's discussion of state-value, distributional-similarity, and learned-transition approaches. Added references and discussion include MoManipVLA, newer foundation/RL policies, and PointNet++; this exceeds a bibliographic refresh.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory motivation, contributions, related work, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. v2 introduces a shared Experiment Settings section and organizes evaluation around six explicit questions. Earlier qualitative experiments and separate appendix analyses are consolidated under Appendix D, producing a broad narrative and structural revision.

P2.justification: v2 switches the main paper to two columns, combines v1's Figures 5 and 6 into Figure 5, and redraws plots with uncertainty displays. It adds the benchmark table, sequential-task Sankey diagrams, and expanded ablation panels, while relocating qualitative figures and reducing the main-text representation visualization. These are extensive display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked a direct policy-aware benchmark and offered limited design and failure analysis. v2's Table 1, sequential-task evaluation, expanded ablations, implementation details, and explicit failure conditions substantially strengthen validation and clarify applicability. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, including undefined uncertainty measures and describing the oracle as an upper bound despite Figure 5 showing N2M exceeding it.
